Comparison

GitHub Copilot vs Cursor

A side-by-side look at GitHub Copilot and Cursor, using the details in each tool profile.

Quick take

Choose GitHub Copilot when your priority is: teams already on GitHub who want AI in their existing editor without switching tools. Choose Cursor when your priority is: heavy agent-driven work across a whole codebase.

  • VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, Xcode, Eclipse, Zed, github.com, GitHub Mobile, GitHub CLI (40+ surfaces)

Key features
  • Inline code completions and Next Edit Suggestions (unmetered on every plan)

Advantages
  • Lowest entry price at $10 and a real free tier
  • works in your existing editor so there is no migration
  • unmetered completions mean everyday autocomplete never costs extra
  • unmatched GitHub-native workflows (PR review, issue-to-PR)
  • The strongest agent experience among IDE-based tools
  • codebase indexing makes context handling noticeably better than extension-based assistants
  • migration from VS Code is effectively free
  • Tab model for multi-line edits is excellent.
Limitations
  • The agent is less capable than Cursor's or Claude Code's on large multi-file tasks
  • the June 2026 shift to credit billing makes costs less predictable for heavy users
  • premium model access is now metered
  • chat context handling is weaker than AI-native editors.
  • Twice the entry price of GitHub Copilot
  • requires switching editors, which some teams will not do
  • usage-credit accounting is opaque and users report unexpected charges (Trustpilot ratings reflect billing complaints)
  • no free tier of real substance

Pricing notes

GitHub Copilot

Free $0 with a monthly allowance of completions and chat. Pro $10/user/mo. Pro+ $39/user/mo. Business $19/user/mo. Enterprise $39/user/mo. As of 1 June 2026 all plans moved to usage-based billing via GitHub AI Credits, calculated on token consumption (input, output, cached); code completions and Next Edit Suggestions remain unmetered on every plan. Free for verified students, teachers and maintainers of popular open-source projects.

Cursor

Hobby free with limited completions and requests. Pro $20/mo. Pro+ $60/mo. Ultra $200/mo. Business $40/user/mo with admin controls, centralised billing, SSO and privacy mode enforcement. Enterprise custom. Higher tiers buy larger included usage pools; heavy use beyond the pool is metered or throttled.

Prices change often. Confirm on the official pricing pages: GitHub Copilot ↗ · Cursor ↗

Frequently asked questions

What is the main difference between GitHub Copilot and Cursor?

GitHub Copilot: The most widely distributed AI coding assistant. Cursor: AI-native code editor built as a VS Code fork, designed around agentic multi-file editing rather than line completion.

When should I choose GitHub Copilot over Cursor?

GitHub Copilot is listed as best for: teams already on GitHub who want AI in their existing editor without switching tools. Cursor is listed as best for: heavy agent-driven work across a whole codebase.

Do GitHub Copilot and Cursor have a free plan?

GitHub Copilot: Yes. Cursor: Yes. Check each official pricing page, as plans change.
